translations.title: Zhongli Attains the Way

To receive this lot is no small matter.
Act with loyalty and integrity, and the emperor will summon you.

traditional.diangu: In the legend recorded here, Zhongli Quan, also called Yunfang and Zhengyang, is a Han general. After defeat, a monk leads him to a cave in the Zhongnan Mountains. Reflecting on worldly success and failure, he leaves office and learns the arts of immortality from Donghua Dijun. He later lives in seclusion, is consulted on affairs of state, and becomes the teacher of Lü Dongbin and a leading figure among the Eight Immortals.

traditional.diangu: Su Qin of Luoyang studies under Guiguzi. His repeated proposals to the ruler of Qin fail, and he returns home penniless to a cold reception from his family. Ashamed, he studies the military text Yinfu with determination, pricking his thigh with an awl to stay awake. He later advocates an alliance of six states against Qin and bears the seals of their chief ministers.

It carries mud in its beak to build a nest.
When the nest finally falls, it must gather mud again.

traditional.jieyue: A thousand schemes, ceaseless effort morning and evening: who knew this undertaking would end in such worry? The image is a swallow carrying mud; matters require exhausting effort and care.

traditional.diangu: Dong Yong loses his mother young and supports his father. Unable to pay for his father's burial, he borrows money and pledges himself to servitude. Heaven, moved by his filial devotion, sends a celestial maiden to help him. She marries him and weaves three hundred lengths of silk to repay the debt, then reveals her identity and returns to heaven. This edition adds that their son later wins first place in the imperial examination.

traditional.diangu: In the story of the Thorn Hairpin, the poor scholar Wang Shipeng marries Qian Yulian and travels to the capital for the examinations. Sun Ruquan tries to force Yulian to marry him. She throws herself into a river but is rescued. Shipeng wins first place and refuses a chief minister's daughter. After repeated hardships, the married couple are reunited.

traditional.diangu: During the Eastern Han, Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao enter Mount Tiantai to gather herbs. They meet two celestial maidens and marry them. After what seems to be half a year, they return home to find that seven generations have passed and nobody knows them. They try to return to the maidens but cannot find the path. The story contrasts deliberate striving with an unexpected encounter.

traditional.diangu: Pei Du, later chief minister under Tang Emperor Xianzong, is poor in his youth. At Xiangshan Temple he finds priceless jade belts and seeks out their owner to return them. traditional.diangu: Zhuge Liang, courtesy name Kongming, studies in seclusion until Liu Bei visits him three times and appoints him military adviser. When Xiahou Dun attacks, Kongming assigns the troops despite Guan Yu's and Zhang Fei's doubts. Victory at Bowang wins their confidence. He later becomes chief minister and is entrusted with the young successor. This is the narrative of the Three Kingdoms tradition.

traditional.diangu: Sun Bin and Pang Juan study under Guiguzi. Jealous of Sun Bin's greater ability, Pang Juan arranges for his feet to be mutilated. Sun Bin feigns madness, escapes to Qi, and becomes its strategist. Pang Juan recognizes but cannot break his battle formation. Sun Bin then uses a decreasing number of cooking fires to lure him to Maling, where the Chinese account says he is killed by hidden crossbowmen.

traditional.diangu: Jiang Wei begins as a Wei officer but is won over by Kongming, who values his courage and intelligence. During his final illness on the northern campaigns, Kongming entrusts Jiang Wei with twenty-four chapters of military writings, described here as 104,112 characters. He hopes Jiang Wei will carry on his unfinished purpose.

traditional.diangu: The woodcutter Wu Ji laughs at Jiang Ziya fishing with a straight hook. Jiang predicts that he will kill someone that day; Wu Ji then accidentally causes a man's death while carrying firewood. Temporarily released to care for his mother, he seeks Jiang's help. Jiang teaches him military arts and, in the legend, evades the divination that would reveal him. Wu Ji later introduces King Wen to Jiang and becomes a general.

traditional.diangu: In Investiture of the Gods, Jiang Ziya reaches seventy-two without worldly success. He receives an astronomical office after exposing a pipa spirit, but fails to dissuade King Zhou from building the extravagant Deer Terrace. He leaves the capital for Xiqi. His wife refuses to accompany him, so they separate. He fishes in the Wei River while waiting for his opportunity.

traditional.diangu: Su Qin's proposals fail at the Qin court, and he returns home exhausted and penniless. His wife continues weaving and his sister-in-law will not cook for him. To travel the world without further trouble,

traditional.diangu: Late in Sui, Li Yuan passes beneath Mount Lintong. Qin Qiong, also called Shubao, is sleeping in a temple to Wu Yuan when cries awaken him. He breaks through the encirclement, drives off the attackers, and saves Li Yuan's family. The tale connects this rescue with Qin's later service as a founding Tang general.

Do not forget the sacred pledge: fulfill it.
Know this divine reminder, and do not treat it lightly.

traditional.diangu: At Dongling Pass, Yang Yicheng sets the Bronze Banner formation, which Qin Shubao cannot defeat. Qin learns that the defending officer Luo Cheng is his cousin and contacts Luo's mother. She directs her son to support the formation openly while secretly helping Qin. Qin breaks the formation and captures the pass.

The sun and moon keep shining in the blue sky.
An upright heart carries a good name throughout the world.

In the legend he defeats them, finds a sword, leaves his wife to enlist, and rises in office. After the Khitan destroy Jin, he proclaims Later Han at Jinyang.

traditional.diangu: Wang Bo longs to attend the rebuilt Tengwang Pavilion at Nanchang. A water deity promises him a favorable wind in a dream. He wakes, finds a boat, and swiftly covers the great distance, then writes the famous Preface to Tengwang Pavilion. The source includes a verse connecting his poetic gift and later immortality with the deity's aid. Its stated reign date conflicts with Wang Bo's lifetime.

traditional.diangu: The source links Li Yuan's accession in 618 with news of Emperor Yang of Sui's death. He establishes Tang and rules for nine years before Li Shimin succeeds him. Beware lest good fortune change into misfortune.
Drunk with wine, you no longer know where you go.
Beneath the pines' shadows, the dream remains dim.

He then understands a verse earlier attributed to his nephew Han Xiangzi: clouds cross the Qinling Mountains; snow fills Blue Pass. The tale ends with Han donating his possessions and becoming an immortal; that ending is legendary.

traditional.diangu: Zhuge Liang admires Jiang Wei, a capable Wei officer devoted to his mother. In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he attacks the city where she lives to draw Jiang away, while sending a disguised double to make Wei believe Jiang has defected. With no way back, Jiang surrenders. Zhuge receives him respectfully, and Jiang becomes sincerely loyal to Shu.

If you ask whether the journey will bring good things,

traditional.diangu: Gao Junbao, son of Gao Huaide, leads two hundred soldiers with supplies to rescue Zhao Kuangyin during a campaign against Southern Tang. At Double-Lock Mountain, the female outlaw Liu Jinding captures him and insists on marriage. The couple then lead their followers through the encirclement to rescue Zhao.

If affairs go wrong, each side makes accusations.
The qin must be heard by someone who understands its music.
Keep to your steady course in quiet, and some clarity may come.

traditional.jieyue: Only a true understanding friend can appreciate you. Leave idle affairs alone; wait for a benefactor and joy follows. The image is meeting a kindred spirit: constancy is favorable.

traditional.diangu: The qin player Boya meets the woodcutter Zhong Ziqi, who understands his music. They become sworn friends and agree to meet again a year later. Boya returns to find Ziqi dead. At his grave, Boya breaks his strings and shatters the qin, asking for whom he could play now that his understanding listener is gone. The tale contrasts plentiful acquaintances with the rarity of a true confidant.

translations.title: Cao Pi Proclaims Himself Emperor

For now, wine and sensual pleasure are indulged to excess.
If the golden rooster brings its message to you,
Wealth, blessings, and emoluments are summoned to your side.

traditional.diangu: Cao Pi, Cao Cao's second son, replaces Emperor Xian of Han and establishes Wei. The source then incorrectly says that Sima Yan deposes Cao Pi seven years later. Historically Sima Yan replaces the later Wei emperor Cao Huan in 265. This note preserves the source's subject while identifying that conflation.

poem: The lofty jeweled pagoda is no ordinary sight.
Its eight clear sides radiate light.
I urge you to set your resolve and bow with devotion.
Through good deeds, heaven bestows blessings.

traditional.jieyue: These blessings are visible to all; there is no need for anxious haste. The commentary attributes them to previously established merit. The image is virtue becoming manifest: affairs are traditionally highly auspicious.

traditional.diangu: Dou Yanshan reaches middle age without a son. His father appears in a dream and tells him to abandon wrongdoing and practice goodness. Dou changes his conduct, helps others, and has five sons. The Three Character Classic praises his upright teaching and the distinction achieved by all five.

translations.title: Six Expeditions Beyond Qishan

Dimly, it seems to spread into flowers within a mirror.
Again and again, one tries to gather what appears there.

traditional.diangu: In the Three Kingdoms tradition, Kongming repeatedly campaigns through Qishan against Wei without final success. The source associates the sixth expedition with his memorial on sending out the troops and his death at Wuzhang Plains. It uses the unfulfilled campaign to illustrate timing, fate, and effort that ends without its intended result; the sequence is the source's literary account.

traditional.diangu: In the Three Kingdoms story, the physician Ji Ping resolves to kill Cao Cao because he controls the emperor. Called to treat a headache, Ji puts poison in the medicine. traditional.diangu: Tao Sanchun, daughter of Tao Hong, marries Zheng En after a martial contest. Their son Zheng Yin marries Wang Yue'e, and all practice martial arts. Learning that Zheng En and Zhao Kuangyin are surrounded during a Southern Tang campaign, Tao leads her son and daughter-in-law to their aid. The two forces meet and return victorious.

translations.title: The Three Teachings Discuss the Way
poem: The insight of buddhas and deities is made known to you.
A deluded person's talk only deepens confusion.
An elder obtains the sacred lot and departs.
Better maintain established ways and wait for the time to come.

traditional.jieyue: The complete set of sacred lots has now spoken. Keep your existing position and wait for the proper time. The image is constancy without movement: waiting is favorable in the traditional reading.
traditional.xianji: This is the concluding or full lot, the end of the collection. Do not act rashly in any matter. Maintain constancy and await the proper time. The traditional text associates Buddhist observances and good deeds with protection.

topics.career: Keep to your current duties. A job change or expansion is discouraged; reconsider when circumstances mature.
topics.marriage: Postpone marriage negotiations. A rushed union may meet reversals; mutual consideration after marriage supports a lasting relationship.
topics.wealth: Seeking wealth is unfavorable, with a pronounced image of loss. Restrain spending and avoid speculative risks.
topics.health: Weakness and susceptibility to illness, including recurrence of old conditions, are indicated. Seek medical attention promptly rather than hiding illness. The traditional text also recommends good deeds and prayers.
topics.family: Maintain the household's established arrangements, avoiding major construction or relocation. Young and old are described as settled; prayers for blessings are recommended.
topics.travel: Travel carries hazards. Postpone it or change the route; take particular care and prepare thoroughly for distant journeys.

traditional.diangu: Representatives of Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism discuss truth together. The source treats this final lot as a return to one's own heart, emphasizing cultivation of character and virtue as the closing message of the collection.
